title: A Weekend at the Night Market（夜市週末）
passage:
Every Friday night, Uncle Wang's family visits the busy night market near their apartment. Last weekend, Amy and her cousin Ben decided to explore the market together. The night market was more crowded than usual because a music festival was happening nearby.
Amy wanted to try the stinky tofu, but Ben thought it smelled too strange to eat. "Just try one bite," Amy said with a laugh. "It's delicious once you get used to it." Ben finally agreed, and to his surprise, he liked it more than he expected.
They also stopped at a drink stand and ordered two cups of bubble tea. The line was so long that they had to wait almost twenty minutes. While waiting, Ben noticed a stall selling handmade bracelets. He picked the cheapest one, but Amy chose the most colorful bracelet on the table.
Near the end of the market, they played a ring toss game. Amy was better at the game than Ben, and she won a small stuffed animal. "You're the luckiest person here tonight!" Ben joked.
Before heading home, they shared a plate of grilled squid. It was hot, but not too spicy for them to finish. Amy said the night market trip was the best part of her whole week. Ben agreed and promised to bring his little sister next time so she could try the delicious snacks too.

vocab.example: The night market is always crowded on weekends.
We love to explore new places during summer vacation.
Many tourists want to try stinky tofu at a Taiwanese night market.
The smell of the fruit was strange to her at first.
Ben agreed to try the food after Amy asked him twice.
There is a fruit stand at the corner of the street.
She ordered a large cup of bubble tea with less sugar.
The shop sells handmade bracelets and necklaces.
Amy bought a colorful bracelet as a gift for her friend.
The night market was full of colorful lights and signs.
He won a stuffed animal by playing the ring toss game.
We shared a plate of grilled squid at the food stand.

grammar: 比較級與最高級 (Comparative & Superlative Adjectives)：兩者比較用「形容詞-er / more + 形容詞 + than」，三者以上比較用「the + 形容詞-est / the most + 形容詞」。例如：The night market was more crowded than usual.；Amy was better at the game than Ben.；Amy chose the most colorful bracelet.；You're the luckiest person here tonight!

too...to / so...that 句型：「too + 形容詞 + to + 原形動詞」表示「太…以致於不能…」；「so + 形容詞 + that + 子句」表示「太…以致於…」。例如：It smelled too strange to eat.；The line was so long that they had to wait almost twenty minutes.；It was not too spicy for them to finish.

reading.q: Why was the night market more crowded than usual?
opts: A music festival was happening nearby
A new store had just opened
reading.ex: 文中提到 The night market was more crowded than usual because a music festival was happening nearby，答案是 B。

reading.q: What did Ben think about the stinky tofu at first?
opts: It smelled too strange to eat
reading.ex: 文中寫道 Ben thought it smelled too strange to eat，答案是 A。

reading.q: How long did Amy and Ben wait in line for bubble tea?
opts: They did not wait at all
reading.ex: 文中提到 they had to wait almost twenty minutes，答案是 B。

reading.q: What did Amy win at the ring toss game?
reading.ex: 文中提到 she won a small stuffed animal，答案是 C。

reading.q: What did Ben promise to do next time?
opts: Bring his little sister to the night market
Play the ring toss game alone
reading.ex: 文末提到 Ben agreed and promised to bring his little sister next time，答案是 A。

grammar.q: The night market was ___ than usual last weekend.
grammar.ex: 兩者比較（平常 vs. 上週末）用 more + 形容詞 + than，故選 more crowded。

grammar.q: The line was ___ long that they had to wait twenty minutes.
grammar.ex: so + 形容詞 + that + 子句 表示「太…以致於…」，故選 so。

grammar.q: Amy chose ___ colorful bracelet on the table.
grammar.ex: 三者以上比較選出最…的，須用 the most + 形容詞，故選 the most。

grammar.q: Amy was ___ at the game than Ben.
grammar.ex: 兩者比較用比較級 better + than，故選 better。

grammar.q: The squid was hot, but not too spicy ___ them to finish.
grammar.ex: too + 形容詞 + for + 人 + to + 原形動詞，表示「對某人來說太…而不能…」，故選 for。

vocab.q: If a place has too many people, it is ___.
vocab.ex: crowded 意指「擁擠的」，符合句意「有太多人的地方」。

vocab.q: To ___ a new place means to travel around and discover it.
vocab.ex: explore 意指「探索」，符合句意「四處遊覽並發現新地方」。

vocab.q: The drink ___ sold bubble tea and other cold drinks.
vocab.ex: stand 指「攤位」，符合句意「賣飲料的攤位」。

vocab.q: Something made by hand, not by machine, is called ___.
vocab.ex: handmade 意指「手工製作的」，符合句意。

vocab.q: A soft toy filled with cotton is called a ___.
vocab.ex: stuffed animal 指「填充玩偶」，符合句意「填充棉花的軟玩具」。
